title: Grateful Dead Live at KQED Studios on 1970-08-30
lineage: FM > Sony TC-366 Reel (concert polyester tape) > CDx3 > HP 9350i > EAC v0.9b4 > CD Wave v1.6 > shntool > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality matrix recording of a 1970 studio session captures powerful performances of Easy Wind, Candyman and Brokedown Palace despite occasional muddiness.
ai_review.review: The set is a short studio‑with‑audience performance that highlights the Dead’s mid‑70s power – Pigpen’s ferocious vocals on “Easy Wind”, a newly‑slowed “Candyman” and a soaring “Brokedown Palace”.  Recording-wise the quad‑broadcast mix is uneven: some spots are muddy or drop out, Phil’s bass sits low and the overall balance wavers, but most listeners find it listenable enough to enjoy the strong musical moments.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (average ★4.0) praise the performances and specific songs, while numerous comments note recording flaws that keep the technical quality at a fair level.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Quad‑broadcast mix from KQED; several reviewers cite muddied/distorted spots, uneven bass levels (Phil low), and occasional drop‑outs. Some note it sounds better than contemporary video tapes but is not a clean soundboard capture.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise studio set that feels like a quick concert; the band builds strong jams around Easy Wind and Candyman, with vocal highlights from Pigpen and Garcia. The pacing is tight despite the limited runtime.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's voice described as mesmerizing on “Candyman” and “Brokedown Palace”; praised for vocal power.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass mixed too low in the broadcast, detracting from the overall balance.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s lead vocals on “Easy Wind” called a ‘busted‑out‑of‑jail’ performance; fans wish for more studio versions of his songs.
